{{nihongo|'''Takuhi Reshi Shrine'''|多久比禮志神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

'''Takuhi Reshi Shrine''' (たくひれしじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|qid=Q132929}} {{ill|Toyama (city)|Q204266|qid=Q204266}} (formerly {{ill|Kaminiikawa District, Toyama|Q11359057|qid=Q11359057}} {{ill|Ōsawano, Toyama|Q8081695|qid=Q8081695}}) Shio. Its {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029|lt=former shrine ranking}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also called '''Shio no Miya''' (しおのみや) after the name of the place where it is enshrined.

During the Meiji era, it was identified as the Shikinaisha Takuhi Reshi Shrine listed in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki}} and was renamed to its current name, but there are several other candidate shrines (ronsha) for the Shikinaisha Takuhi Reshi Shrine.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine enshrines {{ill|Hoori|Q1051960|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hikohohodemi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Toyotama-hime|lt=Toyotama-hime|Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime no Mikoto}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiotsuchi no Oji}}.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, in the 4th month of the 1st year of {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} ({{ill|672|Q30601|qid=Q30601}}), when Hayashi no Sukune Mikaki was traveling upstream on the {{ill|Jinzū River|Q1156518|qid=Q1156518}} by boat, a white-haired old man appeared and told him that a spring by the pine trees on the riverbank ahead produced {{ill|Salt|Q11254|qid=Q11254}} water, and then vanished from sight. Following the old man's words, the party sailed on and found a spring surrounded by a forest. When they boiled down the water, they obtained {{ill|Salt|Q11254|qid=Q11254}}. The white-haired old man was the {{ill|Kunitama|Q9692242|qid=Q9692242|lt=Kunitama deity}}, and this was interpreted as a divine oracle to develop this land. A shrine was built to enshrine this deity, and this is the origin of the shrine. The place name "Shio" (salt) also derives from this event.

During the Meiji era, the shrine was identified as the Shikinaisha Takuhi Reshi Shrine, but "Takuhire" refers to taku cloth (a type of bark cloth), and since this shrine is rather associated with salt, there is also a theory that identifies the Shikinaisha with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Anekurahime Shrine}} (in Toyama City Kureha-machi) or Gofuku Shrine (in Toyama City Gofuku), which are associated with weaving and clothing.
